title: I fish the lake alone every Friday. Tonight something knocked on my boat from underneath.
story:
Something knocked on the bottom of my boat. Twice. Right under my feet.

I was a mile out on the lake, alone, the way I am every Friday. Dead calm. No wind. No signal. The spare life jacket was where it always is, rolled up under the back seat, for the buddy who never comes.

I told myself it was a log. Then it knocked again. Three times, slow and polite, like someone at a door.

So I knocked back. Three times, on the bench.

Everything went quiet. Then the back of the boat dipped, the way it does when a man climbs in.

I didn't turn around. I grabbed the oars and rowed for the dock, counting strokes out loud. Behind me, water dripped onto the floor of the boat. Steady. Close.

"Keep rowing," a voice said, soft and wet, right behind my neck. "You're doing fine."

I hit the dock so hard the hull cracked. I scrambled out and ran for the cabin lights, and I didn't look back until I reached the porch.

The boat was empty. Rocking.

But wet footprints ran past me, up the steps, through my open door.

And the spare life jacket was gone.
premise: solo night fisherman knocks back at something under his boat; it climbs in and rides behind him to shore; invisible wet footprints go into his cabin and the spare life jacket kept for a buddy is gone
